plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of static gain and lag/delay at a moderate input, which determines what u is needed to approach the 0.6 target and how fast to actuate.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y will rise gradually from ~0.21 toward ~0.35-0.55 over 15s with small noisy fluctuations, staying well below 0.85.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of gain at high input and dead-zone threshold, which determines what u is needed to drive y from ~0.19 toward the 0.6 target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with dead-zone/lag is correct, y will rise clearly from ~0.19 toward ~0.3-0.45 during the 7s hold with noisy fluctuations, staying well below 0.85; if y stays flat near 0.19 it indicates very low gain or dead-zone above 0.8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: How y behaves at u=0 (drain rate and time constant) from the current ~0.40 level, which determines integral action, hold effort for 0.6, and safe duration for future pumping tests.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-drain with lag is correct, y will decay gradually from ~0.40 toward ~0.15-0.30 over 20s with ~0.01 noisy jitter, staying well below 0.85; if y holds flat near 0.40 it indicates negligible drain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at intermediate-high u and input needed to hold 0.6, which directly determines controller bias/feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with 1-2s lag is right, y will stay near 0.02 for ~1-2s then rise gradually toward ~0.25-0.40 over 12s at ~0.02-0.03/s with +/-0.01 noise, staying well below 0.85; flat near 0.02 would imply dead-zone above 0.6, fast jump above 0.5 would imply much higher gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether net inflow stays strongly positive at y~0.25-0.5 under u=0.8 and what slope implies for steady-state and u needed to hold 0.6, which determines controller bias, saturation risk, and safe pump duration.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive nonlinear gain with ~1-2s lag is right, y will hold near 0.25 for ~1s then rise at ~0.02-0.03/s toward ~0.38-0.48 over 7s with +/-0.01 noise, still rising at end and staying well below 0.85; flat near 0.25 would imply steady at 0.6 is near 0.25, sharp jump above 0.65 would imply much higher gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at y~0.46-0.55 under u=0.8 and input needed to hold 0.6, which sets controller bias and overshoot risk.
experiments.expected_observation: If increasing nonlinear gain with equilibrium near 0.6 for u=0.8 is right, y will continue from ~0.46 toward ~0.50-0.54 over 4s at ~0.01-0.025/s with +/-0.01 noise, still rising at end and staying below 0.65; flat near 0.46 would imply equilibrium ~0.46 for u=0.8, jump above 0.65 would imply much higher gain and overshoot risk.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold 0.6 around the target level, which sets controller bias/feedforward and determines whether 0.5 holds, decays, or rises.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive nonlinear gain with ~1-2s lag is correct, y will hold near 0.57 for ~1-2s then drift slowly flat to slightly down toward ~0.53-0.58 over 5s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.65; continued fast rise above 0.62 would imply hold-u below 0.5, fast fall below 0.50 would imply hold-u well above 0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise steady-state input to hold 0.6 and local incremental gain around target, which determines controller bias/feedforward and whether 0.5, 0.55 or higher holds without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold-u ~0.5 with ~1-2s lag is right, y will hold near 0.59 for ~1s then rise at ~0.01-0.02/s toward ~0.62-0.65 over 4s with +/-0.01 noise, still below 0.70; flat/decay near 0.59 would imply hold-u >=0.55, fast jump above 0.70 would imply much higher local gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise steady-state input to hold 0.6 and local incremental gain 0.55-0.6, which sets controller bias/feedforward to reach target without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold-u ~0.5-0.55 with small local gain is right, y will rise slowly from ~0.586 at ~0.005-0.015/s toward ~0.60-0.63 over 4s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; flat near 0.585 would imply hold-u >=0.6, fast jump above 0.70 would imply much higher local gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise steady-state input to hold 0.6 and local incremental gain 0.6-0.65, which determines controller bias/feedforward and integral authority to eliminate steady error without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold-u ~0.5-0.6 with small local gain and ~1-2s lag is right, y will hold near 0.59 for ~1s then rise at ~0.005-0.015/s toward ~0.61-0.64 over 3s with +/-0.01 noise, staying below 0.70; flat near 0.59 would imply saturated pump / hold-u >=0.65, jump above 0.70 would imply much higher local gain.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases steady-state level y (positive static gain).
With u=0, level y decays over time toward near-zero due to self-drain rather than holding constant.
Response to a step in u has lag/delay of ~1-2s, not instantaneous.
Effective gain is highly nonlinear: large jump from u=0.4 holding y~0.18-0.20 to u=0.5 holding y~0.588, then shallow but still positive between 0.5 and 0.65, with no hard dead-zone above 0.4.

Steady-state y is monotonic in u and holding y=0.6 requires u~0.50-0.60; u=0.5 holds ~0.588 over 5s and u=0.55 holds ~0.583 over 4s and u=0.6 holds ~0.589 rising to ~0.595 over 4s and u=0.65 rises from ~0.592 to ~0.619 over 3s, and u=0.8 equilibrium is above 0.56.
Sensor noise on y is small relative to the 0.10 control band (std <0.02, typically <0.01), so multi-second averaging reveals true level.
